name: Nitroduck
long_description: We make gene editing easy for all crops. To make pesticides obsolete across vegetables and fruits, enabling coffee to withstand heat waves, making almonds independent of pollinators, pistachios independent of winter chill, and much more. To let breeders create novel, consumer-facing crop varieties like pink pineapples, seedless cherries, and non-browning avocados.
one_liner: Monsanto for yummy crops, but without pesticides

founders.title: Founder/CTO
founders.founder_bio: Co-founder & CTO at Nitroduck (YC F26). I co-led iGEM Brno 2025 to Grand Prize against 330 teams including Stanford and Oxford. I worked at Karolinska Institutet (Amgen Scholars), building nanoparticles for drug delivery to placenta and at CEITEC, where I demonstrated plant telomere proteins bind human DNA more tightly than their own. I'm a National Decathlon Champion and 13x silver medalist in triple jump and high jump.

launches.title: Nitroduck designs new colors, flavors, and disease resistance into fruits and veggies
launches.tagline: Gene-editing made possible for all crops by delivering CRISPR inside a pollen grain, so breeders can actually use it to move distinct traits straight into crosses of their favorite varieties, saving years on their breeding campaigns.
launches.body:
![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=125202&key=user_uploads/2808867/f1373c3e-730f-415e-88e5-bdb4f706ec87)

Creating a new fruit or vegetable variety through **breeding takes 8 - 16 years on average**: hoping for random mutations, then spending ages selecting the good ones. Since each **trait costs $3M**, only essential improvements get made. The industry is only scratching the surface of a **$40B potential royalty market in specialty crops**.

Get that under **8y**, and crops can ship new resistance genes faster than pathogens evolve around them, like patching security bugs faster than hackers can exploit them, so most of the **pesticides stop being needed**. Get that under **4y**, and crop development gets so fast and cheap that **new varieties can follow, or even set, consumer trends**, the way software went from multi-year releases to shipping new features every week.

Accessible genome sequencing and AI can now tell breeders what to aim for, not hope for, and **CRISPR** turns random mutations into chosen ones. From 2026, it's **legal** in 2/3 of the world. The problem is that **gene editing (CRISPR) really only works on corn and a few other crops**, because CRISPR has to go into a single stem cell that's then regrown into a whole plant. That took 14 years to figure out just for corn - the most capitalized crop.

Nitroduck skips the stem cell and **puts CRISPR into a pollen grain**; the grain pollinates a flower, and out comes an edited seed - seamlessly tapping into how breeders already work.

In the last 6 years, as 3M (Matej, Matúš and Miro), **we've engineered 4x more plants than the average plant scientist does in their whole career**. We've enabled gene editing in duckweed, Earth's fastest-growing and smallest plant, which **won us iGEM, the "Olympics of Biotech**," against 330 teams, including Ivy League schools.
